Bitcoin Surges Above $80,000 After Midterm Elections, Shorts Liquidated for $269 Million in One Hour According to Binance market data, Bitcoin is currently trading at approximately $80,510, up 4.2% over the past 24 hours. CoinGlass data shows that $363.67 million in positions were liquidated across the market in the past hour, of which shorts accounted for $268.96 million. BTC liquidations reached $192.26 million (shorts accounted for 96.4%), while ETH liquidations totaled $124.05 million. Over the past 24 hours, total liquidations reached $933.18 million, affecting 120,141 traders. Bitcoin initiated a short squeeze rally after the midterm election results were released. — link

House Democrats Discuss New Crypto Market Structure Bill With Expanded SEC Oversight According to crypto journalist Eleanor Terrett, House Democrats are discussing plans to introduce a broader crypto market structure bill in the next Congress, building on Rep. Maxine Waters’ 2025 Crypto Investor and Consumer Bill of Rights amendment to the CLARITY Act. Citing three industry sources, Terrett reported that the proposal would incorporate previously rejected House Democratic provisions and measures agreed upon by Senate Democrats and Republicans before the September cloture vote. Proposals under discussion include expanding the SEC’s oversight of crypto markets, limiting the CFTC’s role, and potentially adding ethics restrictions on crypto activities by President Trump and other federal officials. Republicans have described the proposal as a “messaging bill.” — link

Strategy’s STRC Touches $100 for First Time Since May, Potentially Reopening Bitcoin Funding Strategy’s perpetual preferred stock STRC briefly touched $100 on November 4 for the first time since May, reaching the minimum price at which the company currently intends to issue new shares under its at-the-market (ATM) program. Strategy repurchased approximately $2.25 billion worth of STRC between July and November 1. SEC filings show that the company used $5.46 billion in net proceeds from STRC ATM sales to purchase Bitcoin in Q2 2026 but made no STRC ATM sales in Q3. With $17.51 billion remaining available under the program as of November 1, the return to $100 could pave the way for renewed STRC issuance to fund Bitcoin purchases, although the latest filing reported no new STRC sales. — link

French Bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa Details $133M Cyberattack via Third-Party Provider, Funds May Have Been Converted Into Crypto French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa disclosed further details on November 4 about a cyberattack reportedly involving approximately $133 million. The attackers gained access to the bank's systems through a third-party service provider's platform and used the bank's own account to transfer funds to other financial institutions. The funds may subsequently have been converted into cryptocurrency through specialized platforms. Regarding reports that €118 million ($133 million) had been stolen, the bank said it could not confirm the exact amount but acknowledged that the figure was of the correct order of magnitude. Some of the affected funds have been blocked, and recovery efforts are ongoing. The bank denied that the attackers gained access through its online banking subsidiary Fortuneo, emphasized that customer assets were unaffected, and said the external attack had been contained. — link
